description: Tell the marketplace what a prior `search` was actually worth: whether you used the answer you bought, partly used it, rejected it, regenerated the work yourself, or declined to buy at all. This is the demand signal publishers act on — an honest "rejected" or "purchase_declined" is as useful as a "used", and reporting nothing leaves the loop blind. Keyless and anonymous: possession of the `searchId` is the only credential, no wallet and no signature. Returns 202 with `{ accepted }` and nothing else by design — the endpoint deliberately cannot confirm or deny that a search exists, so a stale or swept `searchId` is accepted silently rather than 404ing.

outcomes.description: One outcome, or a batch of up to 10. A single-element array IS the single-report case; the route normalizes both the same way.

contentHash.description: Optional "sha256:<64 hex>" over the exact bodyMd the read returned, pinning the outcome to the version you actually read

resourceId.description: Optional uuid of the specific candidate this is about, from the search result. Omit for a verdict on the search as a whole.

status.description: What happened. One of: used | partially_used | rejected | regenerated | purchase_declined.

searchId.description: The `searchId` (uuid) returned by the `search` whose results you are rating

name: report_search_outcome
title: Report a search outcome
